title: Explicit marked internal Hom and exponential adjunction
statement: Use the simplicial sets, standard simplices and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-weil-size-convention]. A marked simplicial set is a pair $(X,M_X)$ with $M_X\subseteq X_1$ containing all degenerate edges; morphisms preserve marked edges. Products mark precisely pairs of marked edges. Write $K^\flat$ for a simplicial set with only its degenerate edges marked and $K^\sharp$ for one with every edge marked. For any marked simplicial sets $X,Y$, define a simplicial set $H(X,Y)$ by $H(X,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}^+}(X\times(\Delta^n)^\flat,Y)$, with operators given by restriction in the simplex parameter. Declare an edge marked exactly when the corresponding map $X\times(\Delta^1)^\flat\to Y$ preserves also the markings of $X\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp$. These formulas define a marked simplicial set, functorial contravariantly in $X$ and covariantly in $Y$. Evaluation induces natural bijections $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}^+}(Z,H(X,Y))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}^+}(Z\times X,Y)$$ for every marked simplicial set $Z$. The bijection is the ordinary simplicial transpose restricted to marking-preserving maps: a transpose preserves markings if and only if evaluation sends every pair of marked edges of $Z$ and $X$ to a marked edge of $Y$. Thus $H(X,Y)$ is the marked internal Hom $Y^X$. The construction and bijection stay in the universe of $X,Y,Z$.

proof.text: For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ define $H(\alpha)(h)=h\circ(\mathrm{id}_X\times\Delta(\alpha))$. A simplicial map sends degenerate edges to degenerate edges, so $\Delta(\alpha):(\Delta^m)^\flat\to(\Delta^n)^\flat$ preserves markings. Thus restriction takes the displayed set $H_n$ into $H_m$. The identity and composition equations follow by composition of these restriction maps. If $h\in H_0$ is a vertex, the edge $s_0h$ is represented by $X\times\Delta^1\to X\xrightarrow{h}Y$. This projection preserves markings even on $X\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, because a marked edge projects to a marked edge of $X$. Hence $s_0h$ is marked. This proves that the given simplicial set with its given subset of edges is a marked simplicial set. These are restriction and degeneracy calculations using the standard simplices and degreewise products, not a horn-filling assertion.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, opening paragraph before Remark 3.1.3.1, printed p.154 (PDF p.172); explicit degreewise verification supplied by the worker.

proof.text: For marked maps $a:X'\to X$ and $b:Y\to Y'$, send $h\in H(X,Y)_n$ to $b\circ h\circ(a\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^n})$. Both precomposition and postcomposition preserve marked maps on the flat product. If $h$ is a marked edge, the same compositions preserve markings on the sharp-interval product, so its image is also a marked edge. These maps commute with restriction in $\Delta^n$, and their identity and composition equations follow from associativity of composition. Therefore $H$ is contravariantly functorial in $X$ and covariantly functorial in $Y$.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, opening paragraph before Remark 3.1.3.1, printed p.154 (PDF p.172); explicit degreewise verification supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Define evaluation in degree $n$ by $E_n(h,x)=h_n(x,\mathrm{id}_{[n]})$. For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, naturality of $h:X\times\Delta^n\to Y$ gives $Y(\alpha)E_n(h,x)=h_m(X(\alpha)x,\alpha)=E_m(H(\alpha)h,X(\alpha)x)$. Thus $E:H(X,Y)\times X\to Y$ is simplicial. If $h\in H_1$ and $x\in X_1$ are both marked, the sharp-extension condition on $h$ applies to the marked pair $(x,\mathrm{id}_{[1]})$ in $X\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp$. It gives $E_1(h,x)\in M_Y$. Thus evaluation is a marked map. For any marked $g:Z\to H(X,Y)$ its untranspose is $F=E\circ(g\times\mathrm{id}_X)$, with $F_n(z,x)=(g_nz)_n(x,\mathrm{id}_{[n]})$.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, opening paragraph before Remark 3.1.3.1, printed p.154 (PDF p.172); explicit degreewise verification supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Conversely, let $F:Z\times X\to Y$ be a marked map. For $z\in Z_n$ define $h_z:X\times\Delta^n\to Y$ in degree $m$ by $(h_z)_m(x,\alpha)=F_m(Z(\alpha)z,x)$, where $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$. For $\beta:[r]\to[m]$, naturality of $F$ makes both sides of the naturality equation equal to $F_r(Z(\alpha\beta)z,X(\beta)x)$, so $h_z$ is simplicial. A marked edge of $X\times(\Delta^n)^\flat$ is $(e,c_v)$, where $e\in M_X$ and $c_v:[1]\to[n]$ is constant at a vertex $v$. Since $Z(c_v)z=s_0(Z(v)z)$ is degenerate and therefore marked, $(h_z)_1(e,c_v)=F_1(Z(c_v)z,e)$ is marked. Hence $h_z\in H_n$. Put $G_n(z)=h_z$. For $\gamma:[k]\to[n]$, the equality $(h_{Z(\gamma)z})_m(x,\alpha)=F_m(Z(\gamma\alpha)z,x)=(H(\gamma)h_z)_m(x,\alpha)$ proves that $G:Z\to H(X,Y)$ is simplicial.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, opening paragraph before Remark 3.1.3.1, printed p.154 (PDF p.172); explicit degreewise verification supplied by the worker.

proof.text: For a marked $z\in Z_1$ and any edge $\alpha:[1]\to[1]$, the edge $Z(\alpha)z$ is marked: $\alpha$ is either the identity or one of the two constant maps, which give degenerate edges. Therefore $(h_z)_1(e,\alpha)=F_1(Z(\alpha)z,e)$ is marked for every marked $e\in X_1$. These are precisely the marked edges of $X\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, so $G(z)=h_z$ is marked. The transpose of a marked $F$ is consequently marked. Conversely, for any simplicial $g:Z\to H(X,Y)$, naturality gives $(g_1z)_1(e,\alpha)=(g_1(Z(\alpha)z))_1(e,\mathrm{id}_{[1]})$. If $g$ is marked, Step 3 gives marked $F$. If its untranspose $F$ is marked, the preceding three-edge calculation shows that $g_1z$ is marked whenever $z$ is marked. Thus the ordinary transpose preserves markings exactly when the untranspose carries every pair of marked edges of $Z$ and $X$ into $M_Y$.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, opening paragraph before Remark 3.1.3.1, printed p.154 (PDF p.172); explicit degreewise verification supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Untransposing the $G$ constructed in Step 4 recovers $F$, since $(h_z)_n(x,\mathrm{id})=F_n(z,x)$. Conversely start with $g:Z\to H(X,Y)$ and put $h=g_nz$. Transposing its evaluation gives in degree $m$ the value $(g_m(Z(\alpha)z))_m(x,\mathrm{id}_{[m]})$. Since $g_m(Z(\alpha)z)=H(\alpha)h$, this value is $h_m(x,\alpha)$, so the original $g$ is recovered. These inverse equations prove the claimed bijection, and the formulas are the usual simplicial evaluation and transpose. Naturality also follows directly from them: for marked $c:Z'\to Z$, $a:X'\to X$, and $b:Y\to Y'$, transposing $b\circ F\circ(c\times a)$ gives at $(z',x',\alpha)$ the value $b_mF_m(Z(\alpha)c_nz',a_mx')$, which is the transpose of $F$ precomposed with $c$ and acted on by $H(a,b)$. Here naturality of $c$ identifies $Z(\alpha)c_n$ with $c_mZ'(\alpha)$. Thus all three naturalities hold. This proves the internal-Hom universal property.

proof.text: Choose the common Grothendieck universe specified in [def-weil-size-convention] containing the degree sets of $X,Y,Z$. Each $(\Delta^n)_m$ is finite. The set $H_n$ is a subset of the countable product of function sets $\prod_{m\geq0}\operatorname{Map}(X_m\times(\Delta^n)_m,Y_m)$ cut out by naturality and preservation of marked edges. A Grothendieck universe is closed under these products, function sets and subsets. Its subset $M_H\subseteq H_1$ belongs to that universe as well. The displayed evaluation, restriction and transpose functions use only these sets. Therefore neither the marked internal Hom nor the adjunction requires a universe enlargement.

lean.statement: theorem marked_internal_hom : ∃ E : ∀ X Y Z : Marked.{u}, (Z ⟶ internalHom X Y) ≃ (product Z X ⟶ Y), (∀ X Y : Marked.{u}, internalHomMap (𝟙 X) (𝟙 Y) = 𝟙 (internalHom X Y)) ∧ (∀ (X X' X'' Y Y' Y'' : Marked.{u}) (a : X' ⟶ X) (a' : X'' ⟶ X') (b : Y ⟶ Y') (b' : Y' ⟶ Y''), internalHomMap (a' ≫ a) (b ≫ b') = internalHomMap a b ≫ internalHomMap a' b') ∧ (∀ (X Y Z : Marked.{u}) (g : Z ⟶ internalHom X Y) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (z : Z.underlying.obj n) (x : X.underlying.obj n), (E X Y Z g).val.app n (z, x) = (g.val.app n z).val.app n (x, stdSimplex.objEquiv.symm (𝟙 n.unop))) ∧ (∀ (X Y Z : Marked.{u}) (F : product Z X ⟶ Y) (n m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (z : Z.underlying.obj n) (x : X.underlying.obj m) (a : m.unop ⟶ n.unop), (((E X Y Z).symm F).val.app n z).val.app m (x, stdSimplex.objEquiv.symm a) = F.val.app m (Z.underlying.map a.op z, x)) ∧ (∀ (X X' Y Y' Z Z' : Marked.{u}) (a : X' ⟶ X) (b : Y ⟶ Y') (c : Z' ⟶ Z) (g : Z ⟶ internalHom X Y), E X' Y' Z' (c ≫ g ≫ internalHomMap a b) = productMap c a ≫ E X Y Z g ≫ b) ∧ (∀ (X Y Z : Marked.{u}) (g : Z.underlying ⟶ (internalHom X Y).underlying), (∀ z ∈ Z.marking, g.app _ z ∈ (internalHom X Y).marking) ↔ ∀ z ∈ Z.marking, ∀ x ∈ X.marking, (g.app _ z).val.app _ (x, stdSimplex.objEquiv.symm (𝟙 ⦋1⦌)) ∈ Y.marking)
